title: Jenkins CI/CD Pipeline
summary: A webhook triggers the controller, which schedules pipeline stages on agents: build, test, scan, push, deploy and smoke test.

nodes.label: Git / SCM
nodes.detail: Hosts code and the Jenkinsfile. Pushes and pull requests send a webhook to Jenkins.

nodes.label: Controller
nodes.detail: Reads the Jenkinsfile, manages credentials and queues, and assigns stages to agents. It should not run builds itself.

nodes.label: Agent
nodes.detail: Runs the pipeline steps in a workspace, often a container or pod created per build.

nodes.label: Build + Test
nodes.detail: Compiles the code and runs unit tests; failures stop the pipeline early.

nodes.label: Scan
nodes.detail: Static analysis and vulnerability scanning of dependencies and images, with quality gates that can fail the build.

nodes.label: Registry
nodes.detail: The tested image is tagged with the commit and pushed to an artifact or container registry.

nodes.label: Deploy
nodes.detail: Updates the environment, for example by changing the image tag in a GitOps repo or applying manifests.

nodes.label: Smoke Test
nodes.detail: Hits health endpoints or runs a short test against the new release, and triggers rollback or alerts on failure.

steps.title: Push triggers the build
steps.text: A commit sends a webhook and the controller starts the pipeline defined in the Jenkinsfile.

steps.title: Agent is allocated
steps.text: The controller queues the job and an ephemeral agent picks it up.

steps.title: Build and test
steps.text: The agent compiles and runs unit tests; any failure ends the run.

steps.title: Scan and publish
steps.text: Quality and security scans gate the build, then the image is pushed to the registry.

steps.title: Deploy and verify
steps.text: The release is rolled out, then a smoke test confirms it is healthy.
